entry_json.definition: a standard by which something is judged or a decision is made
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Choosing the criterion before looking at the data is what separates analysis from selection.
example_sentences: The main criterion for us was how far it was from the station.
Each criterion was weighted equally in the final assessment.

word_family.note: the plural form, used with a plural verb

contexts.text: Choosing the criterion before looking at the data is what separates analysis from selection.
The main criterion for us was how far it was from the station.
Each criterion was weighted equally in the final assessment.

confusables.difference: A standard is a level that must be reached. A criterion is a dimension you judge on, and it may have no threshold attached.
minimal_pair: The criterion was distance from the centre.
The standard requires two years of experience.

entry_json.avoid: Singular criterion, plural criteria. Not "one criteria".

entry_json.definition: a difference between two figures or accounts that should have matched
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The discrepancy between reported and measured hours was too large to be a rounding error.
example_sentences: There was a discrepancy in the bill that took three phone calls to sort out.
A discrepancy of nine per cent was found between the two collection methods.

contexts.text: The discrepancy between reported and measured hours was too large to be a rounding error.
There was a discrepancy in the bill that took three phone calls to sort out.
A discrepancy of nine per cent was found between the two collection methods.

confusables.difference: A difference is neutral and expected. A discrepancy is a difference where you expected agreement, so it needs explaining.
minimal_pair: The discrepancy between the two counts was never resolved.
The difference between the two towns is mainly one of size.

entry_json.avoid: Discrepancy between two things, or in one figure.

entry_json.definition: the level at which something starts to happen or to count
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Where the threshold is set decides how large the problem appears to be.
example_sentences: Once you go over the threshold the tax rate changes completely.
The threshold for inclusion was set before recruitment began.

contexts.text: Where the threshold is set decides how large the problem appears to be.
Once you go over the threshold the tax rate changes completely.
The threshold for inclusion was set before recruitment began.

confusables.difference: A limit is a maximum you must not exceed. A threshold is a minimum at which something begins to apply. They point in opposite directions.
minimal_pair: Above the threshold, the charge applies.
Below the limit, no permit is needed.

entry_json.avoid: Countable. Threshold for inclusion, threshold of pain.

entry_json.definition: a situation where gaining one thing means accepting less of another
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Every policy of this kind involves a trade-off between speed and fairness.
example_sentences: There is always a trade-off between price and how long it lasts.
The trade-off between sensitivity and specificity was made explicit in the design.

word_family.note: to accept less of one thing for more of another

contexts.text: Every policy of this kind involves a trade-off between speed and fairness.
There is always a trade-off between price and how long it lasts.
The trade-off between sensitivity and specificity was made explicit in the design.

confusables.difference: A compromise is an agreement between people, each giving ground. A trade-off is a feature of the situation itself and exists even if only one person is deciding.
minimal_pair: The trade-off is between cost and durability.
The compromise gave each side half of what it wanted.

entry_json.avoid: Hyphenated as a noun, two words as a verb. Trade-off between two things.

entry_json.definition: something that must exist first before something else is possible
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Basic literacy is a prerequisite for everything the rest of the curriculum tries to do.
example_sentences: A driving licence is a prerequisite for that job, which rules me out.
Stable housing proved a prerequisite for engagement with any of the services offered.

contexts.text: Basic literacy is a prerequisite for everything the rest of the curriculum tries to do.
A driving licence is a prerequisite for that job, which rules me out.
Stable housing proved a prerequisite for engagement with any of the services offered.

confusables.difference: A requirement is anything you must satisfy, at any stage. A prerequisite must be in place before you start.
minimal_pair: Stable housing is a prerequisite for treatment.
A second reference is a requirement of the application.

entry_json.avoid: Prerequisite for something, or of something. Not prerequisite to.

entry_json.definition: standing out as the most noticeable or important among many
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The salient feature of the data is not the average but how widely the cases differ.
example_sentences: The most salient thing for me was how quiet it was.
Three salient findings emerged from the analysis of the interviews.

contexts.text: The salient feature of the data is not the average but how widely the cases differ.
The most salient thing for me was how quiet it was.
Three salient findings emerged from the analysis of the interviews.

confusables.difference: Important is about how much something matters. Salient is about how much it stands out, which is a claim about noticing rather than about value.
minimal_pair: The salient detail is the date.
The important consideration is the cost.

entry_json.avoid: Attributive mainly. Use it when you mean prominent, not merely significant.

entry_json.definition: weak and not well supported, especially of a connection or argument
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The link between the two is tenuous enough that the paper should have said so.
example_sentences: The connection felt a bit tenuous to me, honestly.
Evidence for the mechanism remains tenuous outside laboratory conditions.

contexts.text: The link between the two is tenuous enough that the paper should have said so.
The connection felt a bit tenuous to me, honestly.
Evidence for the mechanism remains tenuous outside laboratory conditions.

confusables.difference: Weak is the general word and can describe anything. Tenuous specifically describes a connection or argument that is barely holding together.
minimal_pair: The tenuous link between the two studies was not enough.
The weak signal dropped out every few minutes.

entry_json.avoid: Of links, arguments and grounds. Not of people or physical strength.

entry_json.definition: so small that it can reasonably be ignored
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The effect was statistically detectable and practically negligible, which the summary should have said.
example_sentences: The difference in cost was negligible, so we went with the better one.
Changes below one per cent were treated as negligible in the analysis.

word_family.note: by an amount too small to matter

contexts.text: The effect was statistically detectable and practically negligible, which the summary should have said.
The difference in cost was negligible, so we went with the better one.
Changes below one per cent were treated as negligible in the analysis.

confusables.difference: Small is a comparison of size. Negligible is a judgement that the size does not matter for the purpose at hand.
minimal_pair: The difference was negligible for our purposes.
The room was small but adequate.

entry_json.avoid: Do not confuse with negligent, which means carelessly failing in a duty.

entry_json.definition: much larger or smaller than would be expected given the size of something
entry_json.own_context_sentence: A disproportionate share of the cost falls on the households least able to absorb it.
example_sentences: They spend a disproportionate amount of time on the smallest problems.
Rural areas bore a disproportionate share of the reduction in services.

word_family.note: by more than the expected share

contexts.text: A disproportionate share of the cost falls on the households least able to absorb it.
They spend a disproportionate amount of time on the smallest problems.
Rural areas bore a disproportionate share of the reduction in services.

confusables.difference: Large is an absolute description. Disproportionate is relative and only makes sense once you say what it is out of proportion to.
minimal_pair: The burden was disproportionate to their income.
The burden was large by any measure.

entry_json.avoid: Disproportionate to something. Always name the comparison.

entry_json.definition: increasing steadily as each new amount is added to what came before
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The cumulative effect of small annual cuts is invisible in any single year and enormous over ten.
example_sentences: The cumulative tiredness is what gets you on night shifts.
Cumulative exposure rather than peak exposure predicted the outcome.

word_family.note: to gather more and more over time

contexts.text: The cumulative effect of small annual cuts is invisible in any single year and enormous over ten.
The cumulative tiredness is what gets you on night shifts.
Cumulative exposure rather than peak exposure predicted the outcome.

confusables.difference: A total is one number at one moment. Cumulative describes how that number was built up, adding each period to the last.
minimal_pair: The cumulative figure reached forty thousand by year five.
The total for March was eight hundred.

entry_json.avoid: Attributive. The related verb is accumulate, not cumulate.

entry_json.definition: existing as a permanent and unavoidable part of something
entry_json.own_context_sentence: There is an inherent tension between speed of decision and quality of consultation.
example_sentences: There is an inherent risk in any of this, you cannot design it out.
The limitation is inherent in the method rather than a fault of this study.

contexts.text: There is an inherent tension between speed of decision and quality of consultation.
There is an inherent risk in any of this, you cannot design it out.
The limitation is inherent in the method rather than a fault of this study.

confusables.difference: Built-in means someone put it there deliberately. Inherent means it comes with the nature of the thing and could not be removed.
minimal_pair: The delay is inherent in the process.
The safety catch is built into the handle.

entry_json.avoid: Inherent in something. Not inherent to, in careful British usage.

entry_json.definition: chosen without a clear reason, so that another choice would have been equally valid
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The cut-off is arbitrary, and moving it by one year changes the headline finding.
example_sentences: The rule seemed completely arbitrary to everyone it applied to.
An arbitrary threshold was applied and its effect was tested in the sensitivity analysis.

contexts.text: The cut-off is arbitrary, and moving it by one year changes the headline finding.
The rule seemed completely arbitrary to everyone it applied to.
An arbitrary threshold was applied and its effect was tested in the sensitivity analysis.

confusables.difference: Random has a technical meaning, chosen by a process with no pattern, and it is often a good thing in research. Arbitrary means chosen without justification, and it is usually a criticism.
minimal_pair: The cut-off point was arbitrary.
The sample was random and therefore representative.

entry_json.avoid: Do not use arbitrary when you mean randomised.

entry_json.definition: likely to cause disagreement, because reasonable people take different views
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The most contentious paragraph in the report is the one recommending who should pay.
example_sentences: It is a contentious subject round here, so people avoid it.
The contentious classification was retained with an explanatory note.

word_family.note: disagreement, or a point being argued

contexts.text: The most contentious paragraph in the report is the one recommending who should pay.
It is a contentious subject round here, so people avoid it.
The contentious classification was retained with an explanatory note.

confusables.difference: Controversial suggests public outrage and a wide audience. Contentious is narrower and means specialists disagree, often for technical reasons.
minimal_pair: The definition remains contentious among researchers.
The advertisement was controversial and was withdrawn.

entry_json.avoid: Of issues and claims, not of people, unless you mean argumentative.

entry_json.definition: strong enough to convince someone who did not want to be convinced
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The case for early intervention is compelling and has been for twenty years.
example_sentences: He made a pretty compelling argument, I have to say.
Compelling evidence of harm emerged only after the long-term follow-up.

word_family.note: to force someone to do something

contexts.text: The case for early intervention is compelling and has been for twenty years.
He made a pretty compelling argument, I have to say.
Compelling evidence of harm emerged only after the long-term follow-up.

confusables.difference: Interesting is about attention. Compelling is about persuasion, and it claims the reader had little choice but to accept it.
minimal_pair: The evidence was compelling.
The paper was interesting but proved nothing.

entry_json.avoid: Of evidence and arguments. Compelling reading is a separate and weaker sense.

entry_json.definition: present everywhere in something, so that no part of it is unaffected
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The assumption is so pervasive that it is rarely written down anywhere.
example_sentences: The influence is pervasive, you see it in everything from adverts to job ads.
The effect was pervasive across all four age groups examined.

word_family.note: to spread through every part of something

contexts.text: The assumption is so pervasive that it is rarely written down anywhere.
The influence is pervasive, you see it in everything from adverts to job ads.
The effect was pervasive across all four age groups examined.

confusables.difference: Common is about frequency, how often it occurs. Pervasive is about reach, how completely it has spread through something.
minimal_pair: The attitude is pervasive throughout the organisation.
The complaint is common among new arrivals.

entry_json.avoid: Pervasive throughout or across. Not pervasive in a single instance.

entry_json.definition: possible to do in practice with the resources available
entry_json.own_context_sentence: A scheme can be technically feasible and politically impossible at the same time.
example_sentences: It is not feasible to do all of that in one weekend.
The approach was judged feasible on cost but not on the timescale proposed.

word_family.note: in a way that can be done

contexts.text: A scheme can be technically feasible and politically impossible at the same time.
It is not feasible to do all of that in one weekend.
The approach was judged feasible on cost but not on the timescale proposed.

confusables.difference: Possible means it is not ruled out. Feasible means it could actually be done given the money, time and skills that exist.
minimal_pair: The plan is possible but not feasible on this budget.
It is possible that the trend reverses.

entry_json.avoid: It is feasible to do something. Do not confuse with viable, which is about lasting.

entry_json.definition: able to work successfully and keep going over time
entry_json.own_context_sentence: A service can be launched at any price and is only viable if it survives the second year.
example_sentences: The business was never really viable, we just did not want to admit it.
Only two of the six options remained viable once maintenance costs were included.

word_family.note: the ability to survive and succeed

contexts.text: A service can be launched at any price and is only viable if it survives the second year.
The business was never really viable, we just did not want to admit it.
Only two of the six options remained viable once maintenance costs were included.

confusables.difference: Feasible is about whether it can be done at all. Viable is about whether it can keep going once done. A project can be feasible to build and not viable to run.
minimal_pair: The route is feasible to build and not viable to operate.
The route is feasible with current tunnelling technology.

entry_json.avoid: Viable is about survival over time. Do not use it as a synonym for possible.

entry_json.definition: creating conditions that make a particular outcome more likely
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Open-plan offices are less conducive to concentrated work than to visible activity.
example_sentences: That room is not exactly conducive to studying, with the noise.
Conditions conducive to recovery were absent in most of the wards surveyed.

word_family.note: rare and formal, to lead towards a result

contexts.text: Open-plan offices are less conducive to concentrated work than to visible activity.
That room is not exactly conducive to studying, with the noise.
Conditions conducive to recovery were absent in most of the wards surveyed.

confusables.difference: Helpful is about direct assistance to a person. Conducive is about conditions that favour an outcome, without helping anyone in particular.
minimal_pair: The layout is conducive to conversation.
The librarian was helpful.

entry_json.avoid: Always conducive to. Never conducive for.

entry_json.definition: used to say that a claim can be reasonably defended, though not everyone will accept it
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The reform was arguably the most consequential change of that decade.
example_sentences: It is arguably better than the original, though I know people disagree.
The method is arguably more robust, though the sample does not allow a firm claim.

word_family.note: to give reasons for a position

contexts.text: The reform was arguably the most consequential change of that decade.
It is arguably better than the original, though I know people disagree.
The method is arguably more robust, though the sample does not allow a firm claim.

confusables.difference: Definitely closes the question. Arguably keeps it open and signals that you know a counter-case exists, which is why examiners like it.
minimal_pair: The scheme was arguably a success.
The scheme was definitely a success.

entry_json.avoid: Sits before the phrase it qualifies. It softens a superlative rather than strengthening it.

entry_json.definition: according to what is officially claimed, with the suggestion that the truth is different
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The charge was introduced ostensibly to reduce congestion and largely to raise revenue.
example_sentences: He left ostensibly to spend time with family, but everyone knew.
The programme was ostensibly voluntary, though non-participation carried consequences.

contexts.text: The charge was introduced ostensibly to reduce congestion and largely to raise revenue.
He left ostensibly to spend time with family, but everyone knew.
The programme was ostensibly voluntary, though non-participation carried consequences.

confusables.difference: Apparently means it seems to be the case and you may well believe it. Ostensibly means that is the stated reason and you do not.
minimal_pair: The rule was ostensibly about safety.
Apparently the meeting has been moved.

entry_json.avoid: Always carries a hint of scepticism. Do not use it as a neutral synonym for apparently.

entry_json.definition: every single time, without exception
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Schemes of this size invariably cost more than the figure announced at the start.
example_sentences: It invariably rains the weekend we plan anything outdoors.
The effect invariably appeared within the first forty-eight hours.

contexts.text: Schemes of this size invariably cost more than the figure announced at the start.
It invariably rains the weekend we plan anything outdoors.
The effect invariably appeared within the first forty-eight hours.

confusables.difference: Usually allows exceptions. Invariably claims there are none, which is a much stronger and riskier claim to make.
minimal_pair: The pattern invariably repeats.
The pattern usually repeats.

entry_json.avoid: Sits before the main verb. Only use it when you mean literally every time.

entry_json.definition: used to mark the one point that the whole argument depends on
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Crucially, the two groups differed before the intervention began, not only afterwards.
example_sentences: Crucially, nobody had asked the people who actually use the service.
Crucially, the effect disappeared once household income was controlled for.

word_family.note: the decisive point of an issue

contexts.text: Crucially, the two groups differed before the intervention began, not only afterwards.
Crucially, nobody had asked the people who actually use the service.
Crucially, the effect disappeared once household income was controlled for.

confusables.difference: Importantly marks something worth noting. Crucially marks the point on which everything else turns, so it should appear once in an essay, not four times.
minimal_pair: Crucially, the funding ended in year two.
Importantly, attendance also rose.

entry_json.avoid: Usually opens a sentence with a comma after it. Reserve it for the single decisive point.

entry_json.definition: used to accept a weakness in your own argument before answering it
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Admittedly, the sample was small, but the effect size makes the finding hard to dismiss.
example_sentences: Admittedly I only tried it twice, so I could be wrong.
Admittedly the data predate the reform, which limits what can be claimed.

word_family.note: to accept that something is true

contexts.text: Admittedly, the sample was small, but the effect size makes the finding hard to dismiss.
Admittedly I only tried it twice, so I could be wrong.
Admittedly the data predate the reform, which limits what can be claimed.

confusables.difference: However introduces a contrast with somebody else's point. Admittedly concedes a weakness in your own, which is a different move and reads as more confident.
minimal_pair: Admittedly the evidence is thin, but the direction is clear.
The evidence is thin. However, the direction is clear.

entry_json.avoid: Opens a concession. Pair it with but or nevertheless in the second half.

entry_json.definition: to cause something to begin to exist
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Rapid expansion in the 1960s give rise to a street pattern the city still works around.
example_sentences: That decision give rise to all sorts of problems nobody predicted.
The reform gave rise to a category of worker the legislation had not anticipated.

contexts.text: Rapid expansion in the 1960s give rise to a street pattern the city still works around.
That decision give rise to all sorts of problems nobody predicted.
The reform gave rise to a category of worker the legislation had not anticipated.

confusables.difference: Cause is direct and plain, and works for anything. Give rise to is formal and suits situations and conditions rather than single events.
minimal_pair: Overcrowding gave rise to conditions the inspectors condemned.
The fault caused the power cut.

entry_json.avoid: Followed by a noun. Not by a clause.

entry_json.definition: to depend entirely on one particular thing
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The entire argument hinges on whether the two groups were comparable to begin with.
example_sentences: It all hinges on whether the funding comes through in April.
The conclusion hinges on an assumption the authors state only in a footnote.

contexts.text: The entire argument hinges on whether the two groups were comparable to begin with.
It all hinges on whether the funding comes through in April.
The conclusion hinges on an assumption the authors state only in a footnote.

confusables.difference: Depend on allows several factors, each contributing. Hinge on means there is exactly one, and everything turns on it.
minimal_pair: The verdict hinged on a single document.
The outcome depends on cost, timing and demand.

entry_json.avoid: Followed by a noun or a whether clause. Also spelled hinge upon.

entry_json.definition: to give a reason to be less confident about something previously accepted
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The replication failure cast doubt on a result that had been cited for a decade.
example_sentences: That one story really cast doubt on everything else they had published.
Later measurements cast doubt on the calibration used in the original work.

contexts.text: The replication failure cast doubt on a result that had been cited for a decade.
That one story really cast doubt on everything else they had published.
Later measurements cast doubt on the calibration used in the original work.

confusables.difference: Disprove settles the matter and the claim is dead. Cast doubt on weakens confidence without settling anything, which is usually the honest description.
minimal_pair: The new data cast doubt on the earlier result.
The new data disproved the earlier result.

entry_json.avoid: Past tense is cast, unchanged. Not casted.

entry_json.definition: to make people doubt whether something is true or acceptable
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The delay called into question the department's account of what it knew and when.
example_sentences: That calls into question the whole point of having a policy.
These findings call into question the use of the measure outside clinical settings.

contexts.text: The delay called into question the department's account of what it knew and when.
That calls into question the whole point of having a policy.
These findings call into question the use of the measure outside clinical settings.

confusables.difference: Criticise says something is bad. Call into question says its validity is now uncertain, which is a claim about truth rather than about quality.
minimal_pair: The audit called the figures into question.
The audit criticised the presentation of the figures.

entry_json.avoid: The object can go in the middle or after. No article before question.

entry_json.definition: to disagree with a specific point rather than the whole position
entry_json.own_context_sentence: One might take issue with the definition without rejecting anything else in the paper.
example_sentences: I would take issue with the second point, but the rest I agree with.
Reviewers take issue with the sampling frame rather than with the analysis.

contexts.text: One might take issue with the definition without rejecting anything else in the paper.
I would take issue with the second point, but the rest I agree with.
Reviewers take issue with the sampling frame rather than with the analysis.

confusables.difference: Disagree with can cover a whole position. Take issue with is narrower and more formal, and it signals that you accept the rest.
minimal_pair: I take issue with the third assumption only.
I disagree with the entire approach.

entry_json.avoid: No article before issue. Not "take an issue with".

entry_json.definition: to show that a prediction or claim was correct
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The later data did not bear out the confident projections made at launch.
example_sentences: Everything he said was borne out by what happened afterwards.
The hypothesis was borne out in three of the four regions studied.

contexts.text: The later data did not bear out the confident projections made at launch.
Everything he said was borne out by what happened afterwards.
The hypothesis was borne out in three of the four regions studied.

confusables.difference: Prove is a strong claim of certainty. Bear out means the evidence went the way the claim predicted, which is a more modest and usually more honest statement.
minimal_pair: The results bore out the forecast.
The experiment proved the mechanism.

entry_json.avoid: The past participle is borne, not born. Separable.

entry_json.definition: taking new information into account when reaching a judgement
entry_json.own_context_sentence: In light of the revised figures, the original conclusion is no longer defensible.
example_sentences: In light of what happened last year, I would be more careful.
In light of these findings, the guidance was withdrawn and reissued.

contexts.text: In light of the revised figures, the original conclusion is no longer defensible.
In light of what happened last year, I would be more careful.
In light of these findings, the guidance was withdrawn and reissued.

confusables.difference: Because of names a cause. In light of names information you are now taking into account, which changes a judgement rather than producing an event.
minimal_pair: In light of the audit, the policy was revised.
The policy was revised because of the audit.

entry_json.avoid: British writing often adds the, as in the light of. Both are accepted.

entry_json.definition: apart from the one case you are naming
entry_json.own_context_sentence: With the exception of the smallest district, every area showed the same pattern.
example_sentences: With the exception of Tuesday, I am free all week.
With the exception of two outliers, the values fell within a narrow band.

contexts.text: With the exception of the smallest district, every area showed the same pattern.
With the exception of Tuesday, I am free all week.
With the exception of two outliers, the values fell within a narrow band.

confusables.difference: Except for is plain and works everywhere. With the exception of is heavier and suits formal writing, especially when the exception is being flagged as important.
minimal_pair: With the exception of one site, all met the standard.
Everyone came except for Rob.

entry_json.avoid: Keep the article. Not "with exception of".

entry_json.definition: used to say how far something is true, rather than simply that it is
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The policy worked to the extent that it reduced waiting times, and failed on every other measure.
example_sentences: It helped, to the extent that we finished on time, but nothing more.
The model holds to the extent that demand remains within the sampled range.

chunk.shape: X is true to the extent that Y

contexts.text: The policy worked to the extent that it reduced waiting times, and failed on every other measure.
It helped, to the extent that we finished on time, but nothing more.
The model holds to the extent that demand remains within the sampled range.

confusables.difference: Because gives a reason. To the extent that limits a claim, saying it is true only so far and no further. It is a hedging device rather than a causal one.
minimal_pair: It succeeded to the extent that costs fell.
It succeeded because costs fell.

entry_json.avoid: Followed by a clause. To what extent is the question form.

entry_json.definition: despite the thing just mentioned
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Notwithstanding these limitations, the direction of the finding is consistent across studies.
example_sentences: Notwithstanding the cost, it was the right decision.
Notwithstanding the small sample, the effect exceeded any plausible measurement error.

contexts.text: Notwithstanding these limitations, the direction of the finding is consistent across studies.
Notwithstanding the cost, it was the right decision.
Notwithstanding the small sample, the effect exceeded any plausible measurement error.

confusables.difference: Despite is the everyday word and is safe in any register. Notwithstanding is markedly more formal and can also follow its noun, which despite cannot.
minimal_pair: Notwithstanding the delay, the work was completed.
Despite the delay, the work was completed.

entry_json.avoid: Takes a noun. Very formal, so use it once, not throughout.

entry_json.definition: a large collection of related studies pointing the same way
entry_json.own_context_sentence: A body of evidence built over thirty years is not overturned by one contrary paper.
example_sentences: There is a body of evidence now, it is not just one study.
A body of evidence links the exposure to outcomes measured decades later.

chunk.shape: a body of evidence on X

contexts.text: A body of evidence built over thirty years is not overturned by one contrary paper.
There is a body of evidence now, it is not just one study.
A body of evidence links the exposure to outcomes measured decades later.

confusables.difference: A study is one piece of research. A body of evidence is many, and citing it is a much stronger move in an essay.
minimal_pair: A body of evidence supports the approach.
A study published last year supports the approach.

entry_json.avoid: Takes a singular verb. A body of evidence suggests, not suggest.

entry_json.definition: a complicated consequence that follows from a decision, often unforeseen
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The ramifications of the change were felt in departments that had never been consulted.
example_sentences: Nobody thought through the ramifications of closing that one road.
The legal ramifications were assessed before the policy was adopted.

word_family.note: to branch out into many parts

contexts.text: The ramifications of the change were felt in departments that had never been consulted.
Nobody thought through the ramifications of closing that one road.
The legal ramifications were assessed before the policy was adopted.

confusables.difference: A result is the direct outcome. A ramification is one of the branching, indirect consequences that arrive later and elsewhere.
minimal_pair: The ramifications reached three other departments.
The result was a fall in applications.

entry_json.avoid: Usually plural. Ramifications of something, not for something.

entry_json.definition: someone who argues publicly in favour of an idea or policy
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Proponents of the scheme rarely address who bears the cost during the transition.
example_sentences: He was a big proponent of the whole idea and then went quiet.
Proponents and critics were interviewed using the same schedule.

contexts.text: Proponents of the scheme rarely address who bears the cost during the transition.
He was a big proponent of the whole idea and then went quiet.
Proponents and critics were interviewed using the same schedule.

confusables.difference: A supporter agrees with something. A proponent actively argues for it in public, which is a stronger and more specific role.
minimal_pair: Proponents of the reform published a joint article.
Supporters of the club filled the stand.

entry_json.avoid: Proponent of something. Not proponent for.

entry_json.definition: something that limits what can be done
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The binding constraint on housebuilding is land, not the willingness of anyone to build.
example_sentences: The main constraint for us was time rather than money.
Budget constraints were treated as fixed throughout the modelling.

word_family.note: to limit what someone can do

contexts.text: The binding constraint on housebuilding is land, not the willingness of anyone to build.
The main constraint for us was time rather than money.
Budget constraints were treated as fixed throughout the modelling.

confusables.difference: An obstacle is in the way and might be removed. A constraint is a fixed boundary you must plan within.
minimal_pair: The constraint is the length of the platform.
The obstacle was the objection from two residents.

entry_json.avoid: Countable. Under constraints, within constraints. Not by constraints.

entry_json.definition: a factor that decides what an outcome will be
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The strongest determinant of school attainment remains the income of the household.
example_sentences: The biggest determinant for me was how long the commute was.
Household income was the principal determinant of the outcome measured.

contexts.text: The strongest determinant of school attainment remains the income of the household.
The biggest determinant for me was how long the commute was.
Household income was the principal determinant of the outcome measured.

confusables.difference: A factor is anything that plays a part. A determinant is a factor strong enough to decide the outcome, so it is a much stronger claim.
minimal_pair: Income was the main determinant of the result.
Weather was one factor among several.

entry_json.avoid: Determinant of something. Do not confuse with determined meaning resolute.

entry_json.definition: something measurable used to stand in for something that cannot be measured directly
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Free school meal eligibility is used as a proxy for poverty because poverty itself is hard to record.
example_sentences: Postcode is a rough proxy for income, and a bad one.
Journey time was used as a proxy for accessibility across the network.

contexts.text: Free school meal eligibility is used as a proxy for poverty because poverty itself is hard to record.
Postcode is a rough proxy for income, and a bad one.
Journey time was used as a proxy for accessibility across the network.

confusables.difference: A measure records the thing itself. A proxy records something else and hopes it moves with the thing. Treating a proxy as a measure is where a great many analyses go wrong.
minimal_pair: Postcode is a proxy for income.
Income is measured directly from the tax record.

entry_json.avoid: A proxy for something. Not a proxy of.

entry_json.definition: a standard result used as the point of comparison for everything else
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Without a benchmark the improvement figure has no meaning, however large it looks.
example_sentences: We use last year as the benchmark, which is not ideal.
Performance was reported against a benchmark drawn from the previous decade.

contexts.text: Without a benchmark the improvement figure has no meaning, however large it looks.
We use last year as the benchmark, which is not ideal.
Performance was reported against a benchmark drawn from the previous decade.

confusables.difference: A target is what you are trying to reach in the future. A benchmark is what you compare against, usually from the past or from elsewhere.
minimal_pair: The benchmark was the regional average.
The target was a ten per cent reduction.

entry_json.avoid: Countable. Against a benchmark, not to a benchmark.

entry_json.definition: a division of something into two groups presented as opposites
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The dichotomy between rural and urban hides more variation than it explains.
example_sentences: It is presented as a dichotomy, but most people are somewhere in between.
The dichotomy was replaced by a continuous measure in the revised analysis.

contexts.text: The dichotomy between rural and urban hides more variation than it explains.
It is presented as a dichotomy, but most people are somewhere in between.
The dichotomy was replaced by a continuous measure in the revised analysis.

confusables.difference: A contrast points out a difference between two things that may both be true. A dichotomy claims they are exclusive alternatives, which is often the thing worth challenging.
minimal_pair: The dichotomy forces a choice that need not be made.
The contrast between the two towns is instructive.

entry_json.avoid: Dichotomy between two things. A false dichotomy is the useful critical phrase.

entry_json.definition: the range of matters a person or body has authority to deal with
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The inquiry's remit excluded the funding decisions that had made the failure possible.
example_sentences: That is outside my remit, I would have to pass it on.
The committee's remit was widened after the second complaint.

contexts.text: The inquiry's remit excluded the funding decisions that had made the failure possible.
That is outside my remit, I would have to pass it on.
The committee's remit was widened after the second complaint.

confusables.difference: Responsibility is what you must do. A remit is what you are permitted to deal with, and something can be inside your remit without being your responsibility.
minimal_pair: Housing is within the remit of the committee.
Reporting the fault is the caretaker's responsibility.

entry_json.avoid: Chiefly British. Within or outside a remit. The verb remit means something different.

entry_json.definition: the path something is following and where it is heading
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The trajectory of emissions matters more than any single year's total.
example_sentences: Her career took a completely different trajectory after that year abroad.
The trajectory over the period suggests the earlier peak will not be repeated.

contexts.text: The trajectory of emissions matters more than any single year's total.
Her career took a completely different trajectory after that year abroad.
The trajectory over the period suggests the earlier peak will not be repeated.

confusables.difference: A trend is a direction observed in past data. A trajectory adds the sense of continuing forward, so it implies a prediction.
minimal_pair: The trajectory points to a shortfall by 2030.
The trend over the last decade was upward.

entry_json.avoid: Countable. On a trajectory, not in one.

entry_json.definition: an event that speeds up a change that was already possible
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The closure was the catalyst rather than the cause, since the decline had begun years earlier.
example_sentences: That conversation was the catalyst for me leaving.
The report acted as a catalyst for reforms that had been proposed for a decade.

word_family.note: to trigger or speed up a change

contexts.text: The closure was the catalyst rather than the cause, since the decline had begun years earlier.
That conversation was the catalyst for me leaving.
The report acted as a catalyst for reforms that had been proposed for a decade.

confusables.difference: A cause produces the effect. A catalyst only accelerates something already able to happen, so using it correctly is a claim about timing rather than about origin.
minimal_pair: The strike was the catalyst for negotiations.
Underfunding was the cause of the dispute.

entry_json.avoid: A catalyst for something. Not a catalyst of.

entry_json.definition: something produced incidentally while making or doing something else
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Social contact is a by-product of the commute that remote work quietly removed.
example_sentences: A nice by-product of cycling is that I sleep much better.
Heat is a by-product of the process and is currently vented rather than used.

contexts.text: Social contact is a by-product of the commute that remote work quietly removed.
A nice by-product of cycling is that I sleep much better.
Heat is a by-product of the process and is currently vented rather than used.

confusables.difference: A result is what the activity was aimed at. A by-product is what came out alongside it, without being the point.
minimal_pair: Warmth is a by-product of the reaction.
The result was a purer compound.

entry_json.avoid: Hyphenated in British usage. By-product of something.

entry_json.definition: the size of something, especially of a change or an effect
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The direction of the effect is agreed and its magnitude is not.
example_sentences: I did not appreciate the magnitude of the problem until I saw the figures.
The magnitude of the reduction exceeded every published forecast.

contexts.text: The direction of the effect is agreed and its magnitude is not.
I did not appreciate the magnitude of the problem until I saw the figures.
The magnitude of the reduction exceeded every published forecast.

confusables.difference: Scale is about how far something extends, how many places or people. Magnitude is about how large the quantity is.
minimal_pair: The magnitude of the fall was eleven per cent.
The scale of the outbreak covered four counties.

entry_json.avoid: Uncountable in this sense. An order of magnitude means a factor of ten.

entry_json.definition: a value far away from all the others in a set of data
entry_json.own_context_sentence: One outlier can shift an average enough to reverse the conclusion drawn from it.
example_sentences: That one month was an outlier, the rest were all similar.
Two outliers were retained and their effect reported separately.

contexts.text: One outlier can shift an average enough to reverse the conclusion drawn from it.
That one month was an outlier, the rest were all similar.
Two outliers were retained and their effect reported separately.

confusables.difference: An exception is a case a rule does not cover. An outlier is a data point far from the rest, and it may follow the rule perfectly.
minimal_pair: The outlier was nine standard deviations from the mean.
The exception applies to buildings under three storeys.

entry_json.avoid: Countable. One word.

entry_json.definition: strong enough to hold up when tested in different ways
entry_json.own_context_sentence: A robust finding survives a change of method, not just a change of author.
example_sentences: The system is pretty robust, it has not gone down in two years.
The result was robust to every alternative specification the authors tried.

word_family.note: the quality of holding up under testing

contexts.text: A robust finding survives a change of method, not just a change of author.
The system is pretty robust, it has not gone down in two years.
The result was robust to every alternative specification the authors tried.

confusables.difference: Strong describes the size of an effect. Robust describes whether it survives being tested differently, which is a claim about reliability.
minimal_pair: The finding is robust to changes in the sample.
The effect is strong in every group.

entry_json.avoid: Robust to a change, not robust against.

entry_json.definition: so small as to be barely worth taking into account
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The improvement was marginal and the cost of achieving it was not.
example_sentences: The difference was marginal, so we did not bother switching.
Marginal gains in accuracy did not justify the additional processing time.

word_family.note: the edge or the amount by which something differs

contexts.text: The improvement was marginal and the cost of achieving it was not.
The difference was marginal, so we did not bother switching.
Marginal gains in accuracy did not justify the additional processing time.

confusables.difference: Minor means unimportant in itself. Marginal means small relative to something else, usually to the effort or cost of getting it.
minimal_pair: The marginal benefit did not cover the marginal cost.
The change was a minor one and passed without comment.

entry_json.avoid: In economics it means the effect of one more unit, which is a technical sense.

entry_json.definition: belonging to the nature of something rather than added from outside
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Intrinsic motivation outlasts every reward scheme designed to replace it.
example_sentences: There is an intrinsic value in doing it well, whatever anyone pays.
Intrinsic and extrinsic motivation were measured separately in the study.

contexts.text: Intrinsic motivation outlasts every reward scheme designed to replace it.
There is an intrinsic value in doing it well, whatever anyone pays.
Intrinsic and extrinsic motivation were measured separately in the study.

confusables.difference: Extrinsic comes from outside, such as pay or grades. Intrinsic comes from within, such as interest or satisfaction. They can pull against each other.
minimal_pair: Intrinsic motivation kept them practising.
Extrinsic rewards raised output briefly.

entry_json.avoid: Intrinsic to something. Very close to inherent, but intrinsic is preferred for value and motivation.

entry_json.definition: fitting together logically, so that each part supports the rest
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The policy is well intentioned and not coherent, because two of its aims work against each other.
example_sentences: He was not very coherent at that point, to be fair to him.
A coherent account of the mechanism did not emerge until the third study.

word_family.note: how the parts of a text connect

contexts.text: The policy is well intentioned and not coherent, because two of its aims work against each other.
He was not very coherent at that point, to be fair to him.
A coherent account of the mechanism did not emerge until the third study.

confusables.difference: Clear means easy to understand. Coherent means the parts do not contradict each other. Something can be perfectly clear and completely incoherent.
minimal_pair: The argument was clear but not coherent.
The instructions were clear and easy to follow.

entry_json.avoid: Of arguments and accounts. Coherence and cohesion are different things in writing assessment.

entry_json.definition: done according to a fixed plan, so that nothing is left to chance
entry_json.own_context_sentence: A systematic search finds the studies that disagree with you as well as those that do not.
example_sentences: We need a more systematic way of recording these, it is all over the place.
A systematic review of the literature preceded the primary data collection.

contexts.text: A systematic search finds the studies that disagree with you as well as those that do not.
We need a more systematic way of recording these, it is all over the place.
A systematic review of the literature preceded the primary data collection.

confusables.difference: Thorough means nothing was missed. Systematic means a stated method was followed, which allows someone else to repeat it.
minimal_pair: The systematic review followed a published protocol.
The check was thorough and took two days.

entry_json.avoid: Do not confuse with systemic, which means affecting a whole system.

entry_json.definition: found everywhere, to the point of being unremarkable
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Screens became ubiquitous before anyone had decided whether that was desirable.
example_sentences: Those little scooters are ubiquitous now, they are everywhere.
The material is ubiquitous in packaging and almost never recovered.

contexts.text: Screens became ubiquitous before anyone had decided whether that was desirable.
Those little scooters are ubiquitous now, they are everywhere.
The material is ubiquitous in packaging and almost never recovered.

confusables.difference: Common is about frequency and allows plenty of places without it. Ubiquitous claims it is present essentially everywhere.
minimal_pair: Mobile payment is ubiquitous in the capital.
Cash payment is still common in rural shops.

entry_json.avoid: No comparative. Something is ubiquitous or it is not.

entry_json.definition: being the most common or most widely accepted at a particular time
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The prevailing view in the 1980s was almost the reverse of what is assumed today.
example_sentences: The prevailing mood in the office was not great that week.
The prevailing interpretation was challenged by evidence published in 2019.

word_family.note: to be most common, or to win in the end

contexts.text: The prevailing view in the 1980s was almost the reverse of what is assumed today.
The prevailing mood in the office was not great that week.
The prevailing interpretation was challenged by evidence published in 2019.

confusables.difference: Popular means many people like it. Prevailing means it is the dominant view at the moment, whether or not anyone likes it.
minimal_pair: The prevailing view was pessimistic.
The popular choice was the cheaper option.

entry_json.avoid: Attributive. Prevailing wind is a separate literal use.

entry_json.definition: large enough to be noticed and measured
entry_json.own_context_sentence: There was no appreciable difference between the two groups at the six-month point.
example_sentences: I have not seen any appreciable change since they resurfaced it.
An appreciable reduction in waiting time appeared only in the second year.

word_family.note: by an amount that can be noticed

contexts.text: There was no appreciable difference between the two groups at the six-month point.
I have not seen any appreciable change since they resurfaced it.
An appreciable reduction in waiting time appeared only in the second year.

confusables.difference: Significant has a technical meaning in statistics that does not mean large. Appreciable is about size and is the safer word when you mean noticeable.
minimal_pair: There was an appreciable rise of nine per cent.
The rise was statistically significant but very small.

entry_json.avoid: Do not confuse with appreciative, which means grateful.

entry_json.definition: to keep an important fact in your thinking while you consider something else
entry_json.own_context_sentence: It is worth bear in mind that the figures cover only households already in the scheme.
example_sentences: Bear in mind that the last bus is at eleven.
Readers should bear in mind that the sample excluded anyone under eighteen.
collocations: it is worth bearing in mind

contexts.text: It is worth bear in mind that the figures cover only households already in the scheme.
Bear in mind that the last bus is at eleven.
Readers should bear in mind that the sample excluded anyone under eighteen.

confusables.difference: Remember is about recall, bringing something back. Bear in mind is about holding something present while you judge, which is why it fits qualifications and caveats.
minimal_pair: Bear in mind that the data are three years old.
Remember to send the form before Friday.

entry_json.avoid: Followed by that or a noun. Not "bear on mind".

entry_json.definition: in conflict with, so that both cannot be true or both cannot be done
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The stated aim is at odds with the funding formula that accompanies it.
example_sentences: His account is at odds with what everyone else remembers.
The finding is at odds with two earlier studies using the same instrument.

chunk.shape: X is at odds with Y

contexts.text: The stated aim is at odds with the funding formula that accompanies it.
His account is at odds with what everyone else remembers.
The finding is at odds with two earlier studies using the same instrument.

confusables.difference: Different from is neutral and allows both to stand. At odds with says they contradict each other, so one must give way.
minimal_pair: The result is at odds with the theory.
This method is different from the one used earlier.

entry_json.avoid: Plural odds, no article. Not "at odd with".

entry_json.definition: happening together with something else and working alongside it
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Charging schemes work only in tandem with a service that people can switch to.
example_sentences: The two things happened in tandem with each other, which made it hard to separate them.
The training was delivered in tandem with changes to the recording system.

chunk.shape: X operates in tandem with Y

contexts.text: Charging schemes work only in tandem with a service that people can switch to.
The two things happened in tandem with each other, which made it hard to separate them.
The training was delivered in tandem with changes to the recording system.

confusables.difference: At the same time as is only about timing. In tandem with adds that the two work together deliberately towards the same end.
minimal_pair: The measures were introduced in tandem with each other.
The roadworks began at the same time as the festival.

entry_json.avoid: Formal. Not "in tandem to".

entry_json.definition: mostly true, though not in every case
entry_json.own_context_sentence: For the most part the pattern is consistent, with one region behaving differently throughout.
example_sentences: For the most part I enjoyed it, though the last week was hard.
For the most part, participants completed the diary without prompting.

contexts.text: For the most part the pattern is consistent, with one region behaving differently throughout.
For the most part I enjoyed it, though the last week was hard.
For the most part, participants completed the diary without prompting.

confusables.difference: Mostly is a single adverb and sits with the verb. For the most part is a phrase that frames a whole clause and is more formal in writing.
minimal_pair: For the most part, the results agreed.
The results mostly agreed.

entry_json.avoid: Fixed. Not "for most part".

entry_json.definition: in more than half of cases, though far from always
entry_json.own_context_sentence: More often than not, the cheapest tender turns out not to be the cheapest project.
example_sentences: More often than not I end up walking because the bus never comes.
More often than not, the effect appeared in the first week rather than later.

contexts.text: More often than not, the cheapest tender turns out not to be the cheapest project.
More often than not I end up walking because the bus never comes.
More often than not, the effect appeared in the first week rather than later.

confusables.difference: Usually suggests a strong majority of occasions. More often than not claims only a simple majority, so it is the more cautious of the two.
minimal_pair: More often than not the delay is under ten minutes.
The delay is usually under ten minutes.

entry_json.avoid: Fixed order. It is a comparison, so keep than.

entry_json.definition: across the whole span of time covered by a chart or table
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Car ownership rose steadily over the period shown, while bus use fell in every year.
example_sentences: Over the period shown it more or less doubled, from what I can see.
Expenditure on housing increased over the period shown in all four categories.

contexts.text: Car ownership rose steadily over the period shown, while bus use fell in every year.
Over the period shown it more or less doubled, from what I can see.
Expenditure on housing increased over the period shown in all four categories.

confusables.difference: During this time is vague and could mean any stretch. Over the period shown points explicitly at the chart, which is what a Task 1 answer needs.
minimal_pair: Sales trebled over the period shown.
Sales trebled during this time.

entry_json.avoid: Use it when describing a figure with a stated time axis.

entry_json.definition: to stay at roughly the same level, with only small movements
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Rail use remain broadly stable while road use rose by a third over the same years.
example_sentences: Numbers remain broadly stable for about a decade, then jumped.
Participation remain broadly stable across all age groups except the youngest.

contexts.text: Rail use remain broadly stable while road use rose by a third over the same years.
Numbers remain broadly stable for about a decade, then jumped.
Participation remain broadly stable across all age groups except the youngest.

confusables.difference: Stay the same claims no change at all, which a chart almost never shows. Remain broadly stable allows small movement and is the accurate phrase.
minimal_pair: The figure remained broadly stable at nine per cent.
The figure stayed the same at exactly nine per cent.

entry_json.avoid: Broadly is the hedge that makes the claim defensible. Do not drop it.

entry_json.definition: a rise large enough to stand out clearly on a chart
entry_json.own_context_sentence: There was a marked increase in private rental costs after the second year shown.
example_sentences: There was a marked increase in people cycling once they put the lane in.
A marked increase in applications followed the removal of the fee.

chunk.shape: there was a marked increase in X

contexts.text: There was a marked increase in private rental costs after the second year shown.
There was a marked increase in people cycling once they put the lane in.
A marked increase in applications followed the removal of the fee.

confusables.difference: A slight increase is small and might be noise. A marked increase is large enough that a reader would see it without being told.
minimal_pair: There was a marked increase of twenty per cent.
There was a slight increase of half a per cent.

entry_json.avoid: Increase in something, never increase of something when naming the category.

entry_json.definition: increased to more than twice the original amount
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Spending on the scheme more than doubled between the first and last years shown.
example_sentences: The rent has more than doubled since we moved in.
Enrolment more than doubled over the decade covered by the figures.

chunk.shape: X more than doubled between A and B

contexts.text: Spending on the scheme more than doubled between the first and last years shown.
The rent has more than doubled since we moved in.
Enrolment more than doubled over the decade covered by the figures.

confusables.difference: Increased by half means it rose by fifty per cent of the original. More than doubled means it rose by over a hundred per cent. Confusing by and to here is a very common error.
minimal_pair: Output more than doubled, from four to nine units.
Output increased by half, from four to six units.

entry_json.avoid: Use from and to for the two values. Increase by an amount, increase to a level.

entry_json.definition: measured as a raw quantity rather than as a share or a rate
entry_json.own_context_sentence: In absolute terms the largest rise was in the biggest city, though the fastest growth was elsewhere.
example_sentences: In absolute terms it is more money, but as a share of income it is less.
In absolute terms, emissions fell while emissions per unit of output rose.

contexts.text: In absolute terms the largest rise was in the biggest city, though the fastest growth was elsewhere.
In absolute terms it is more money, but as a share of income it is less.
In absolute terms, emissions fell while emissions per unit of output rose.

confusables.difference: In absolute terms compares raw quantities. In relative terms compares shares or rates. Charts routinely show one rising while the other falls, and saying which you mean is essential.
minimal_pair: In absolute terms the total rose.
In relative terms the share fell.

entry_json.avoid: Plural terms. Pair it with in relative terms in the same paragraph.

entry_json.definition: to make an existing argument or claim more convincing
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The independent replication lend weight to a conclusion that had rested on one study.
example_sentences: Having her say it too really lend weight to the whole thing.
These findings lend weight to the case for earlier screening.

contexts.text: The independent replication lend weight to a conclusion that had rested on one study.
Having her say it too really lend weight to the whole thing.
These findings lend weight to the case for earlier screening.

confusables.difference: Prove settles the matter. Lend weight to adds support to something already argued, without claiming to settle it, which is usually the accurate description.
minimal_pair: The data lend weight to the hypothesis.
The data prove the hypothesis.

entry_json.avoid: Data lend, treated as plural in formal academic writing. Weight is uncountable here.

entry_json.definition: to point out an important difference between two things people confuse
entry_json.own_context_sentence: It is worth draw a distinction between what the policy intends and what it funds.
example_sentences: You have to draw a distinction between being busy and being productive.
The authors draw a distinction between participation and attainment throughout.

chunk.shape: draw a distinction between X and Y

contexts.text: It is worth draw a distinction between what the policy intends and what it funds.
You have to draw a distinction between being busy and being productive.
The authors draw a distinction between participation and attainment throughout.

confusables.difference: Compare looks at similarities and differences together. Drawing a distinction is specifically insisting that two things be kept apart, usually because readers merge them.
minimal_pair: The paper draws a distinction between the two measures.
The paper compares the two measures.

entry_json.avoid: Between two things joined by and. Not "distinction of".

entry_json.definition: taking everything relevant into account before reaching a judgement
entry_json.own_context_sentence: All things considered, the scheme delivered less than promised and more than its critics expected.
example_sentences: All things considered, I think it went quite well.
All things considered, the evidence favours the earlier intervention.

contexts.text: All things considered, the scheme delivered less than promised and more than its critics expected.
All things considered, I think it went quite well.
All things considered, the evidence favours the earlier intervention.

confusables.difference: In conclusion announces the end of a text. All things considered announces a judgement that weighs competing points, so it fits the last paragraph of an argument essay far better.
minimal_pair: All things considered, the cost is justified.
In conclusion, three factors have been discussed.

entry_json.avoid: A participle phrase. Follow it with a comma and a full clause.

entry_json.definition: used to add a second, weaker case after the main one
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Manufacturing and, to a lesser extent, construction accounted for the fall in employment.
example_sentences: It was mainly the price and to a lesser extent the location.
Age and, to a lesser extent, prior education predicted completion.

contexts.text: Manufacturing and, to a lesser extent, construction accounted for the fall in employment.
It was mainly the price and to a lesser extent the location.
Age and, to a lesser extent, prior education predicted completion.

confusables.difference: Also adds a second item as an equal. To a lesser extent adds it while ranking it below the first, which is more precise and reads as more controlled.
minimal_pair: Rail and, to a lesser extent, bus use recovered.
Rail use recovered and bus use also recovered.

entry_json.avoid: Set it off with commas when it interrupts. Lesser, not less.

entry_json.definition: able to be defended against criticism
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The position is no longer tenable once the second dataset is taken into account.
example_sentences: That argument is just not tenable any more.
Neither interpretation remained tenable after the reanalysis.

word_family.note: whether a position can be held

contexts.text: The position is no longer tenable once the second dataset is taken into account.
That argument is just not tenable any more.
Neither interpretation remained tenable after the reanalysis.

confusables.difference: Correct says the claim is true. Tenable says it can be defended, which is a weaker and more careful claim, and it is what most academic writing can honestly assert.
minimal_pair: The hypothesis is tenable on the evidence available.
The calculation is correct.

entry_json.avoid: Of positions and arguments, not of facts. The negative untenable is more common.

entry_json.definition: suggesting that something is probably the case, without proving it
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The pattern is indicative of a supply problem rather than a fall in demand.
example_sentences: The symptoms were indicative of something more serious, so they referred her.
The distribution is indicative of measurement error rather than of real variation.

contexts.text: The pattern is indicative of a supply problem rather than a fall in demand.
The symptoms were indicative of something more serious, so they referred her.
The distribution is indicative of measurement error rather than of real variation.

confusables.difference: Proof of settles the question. Indicative of only points towards a conclusion, which is what evidence usually does and what careful writing should say.
minimal_pair: The rise is indicative of underlying demand.
The receipt is proof of purchase.

entry_json.avoid: Always with of. Not indicative for.

entry_json.definition: dealing with the real content of something rather than with its form
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The revisions were presentational, and no substantive change was made to the recommendations.
example_sentences: There was nothing substantive in the reply, just an acknowledgement.
Substantive differences between the two protocols were limited to the follow-up period.

word_family.note: the real content or importance of something

contexts.text: The revisions were presentational, and no substantive change was made to the recommendations.
There was nothing substantive in the reply, just an acknowledgement.
Substantive differences between the two protocols were limited to the follow-up period.

confusables.difference: Substantial means large in amount. Substantive means concerning the actual substance rather than the wording. They look alike and mean quite different things.
minimal_pair: No substantive change was made to the policy.
A substantial sum was allocated to the project.

entry_json.avoid: Do not use it as a fancier spelling of substantial.

I do not know anything about that.

entry_json.avoid: Always follow with but and an attempt. It is a hedge, not a refusal.

entry_json.definition: used to add a contrasting point immediately after making one
entry_json.own_context_sentence: That said, the newer estates do have proper pavements, which the old ones never did.
example_sentences: That said, I would not want to do it in winter.
That said, only one region was covered by the survey.

contexts.text: That said, the newer estates do have proper pavements, which the old ones never did.
That said, I would not want to do it in winter.
That said, only one region was covered by the survey.

confusables.difference: But sits inside a sentence and joins two clauses. That said starts a new one, which is easier to manage under pressure and sounds more deliberate.
minimal_pair: It is slow. That said, it always arrives.
It is slow but it always arrives.

entry_json.avoid: A shortened participle phrase. Follow it with a comma.

vocab_new.lemma: I would not go that far

entry_json.headword: I would not go that far
entry_json.definition: used to reject an overstatement while agreeing with the direction
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I would not go that far, though it is certainly worse than it was five years ago.
example_sentences: I would not go that far, but I did find it disappointing.
I would not go that far, although the trend is clearly downward.
collocations: I would not go that far
I would not go so far as to say
I would stop short of saying

chunk.fixed_part: I would not go that far

contexts.gap_span: I would not go that far

confusables.difference: No rejects the point entirely. I would not go that far accepts the direction and rejects only the strength, which is a much more precise disagreement.
minimal_pair: I would not go that far, but it has declined.
No, it has not declined.

entry_json.avoid: Follow with but or though. It is a partial disagreement, so say what you do accept.

entry_json.definition: used before something that is a coincidence or mildly surprising
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Funnily enough, the quietest street in the area is the one nearest the station.
example_sentences: Funnily enough, I was thinking about that this morning.
Funnily enough, the two independent teams reached the same figure.

contexts.text: Funnily enough, the quietest street in the area is the one nearest the station.
Funnily enough, I was thinking about that this morning.
Funnily enough, the two independent teams reached the same figure.

confusables.difference: Surprisingly is a plain adverb and works in writing. Funnily enough is warmer and conversational, and it signals a coincidence rather than a genuine surprise.
minimal_pair: Funnily enough, we ended up in the same class.
Surprisingly, we ended up in the same class.

entry_json.avoid: Enough follows the adverb. Speaking and informal writing only.

vocab_new.lemma: it is one of those things

entry_json.headword: it is one of those things
entry_json.definition: used to accept something mildly annoying that cannot be helped
entry_json.own_context_sentence: It is one of those things, the bus is late and there is nothing anyone can do about it.
example_sentences: It is one of those things you only notice once you have moved away.
It is one of those things that never appears in the official figures.
collocations: it is one of those things

chunk.shape: it is one of those things CLAUSE

contexts.text: It is one of those things, the bus is late and there is nothing anyone can do about it.

contexts.gap_span: It is one of those things
